messages:
Priya S.: Escalation from Support — ACME (acct acme-prod) reporting p99 spikes ~16s on Dedicated pool eu-west-1 during billing-window (09:30 UTC). Customer says failures + 500s increase. No model/version changes on their side. Can SRE triage? @Evan @oncall-lead

Evan: copying logs now. Any fast mitigations we can push while we dig in?

support-bot: ALERT: 2026-03-17T09:36Z p99=16.2s p95=6.4s error_rate=3.1% attach_delay spikes observed; provisioning_queue=42; attach_errors=auth-502: 37 in 12m

Evan: quick paste of relevant attach logs (sanitized):
```
[09:33:12] attach_request pool=dedicated-eu-west-1 owner=acme-prod token_check=ok
[09:33:12] provisioner: queue_wait_ms=8420 attach_latency_ms=15234 result=ok
[09:34:05] attach_request failed owner=acme-prod err=auth-502 backend=token-vault
[09:34:05] provisioner: allocate_node timeout=30000 reason=pod_image_pull
[09:35:40] attach_request pool=dedicated-eu-west-1 queue_pos=27
```

Priya S.: Customer also reported a billing job kicking off at 09:30 that spikes infra consumption across several accounts in the org. Could be fairshare interaction.

oncall-lead: hypothesis: fairshare/win-billing-window boosted parallel attach attempts -> provisioner queue starved -> attach latencies and some auth retries timed out leading to 502s. Need repro and short-term fallback.

Evan: repro steps I'm running locally (will paste commands):
```
# reproduce attach pressure
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" -H "X-Model: rdl-4x" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
```
This reproduces attach queues + p99 bump in ~2-4m in our staging pool when concurrent attach >30.

Customer Ops: ACME wants a mitigation ASAP — they risk user-facing errors. They asked if we can route traffic to hosted fallback for 30m.

Priya S.: Suggested immediate mitigations to try (ordered):
1) Route ACME to hosted fallback / route-override (low friction) — support action.
2) Increase min_reserved for their dedicated pool from 0->2 to ensure warm capacity (console change).
3) Temporarily lower model variant (rdl-4x -> rdl-2x) via rollout pin for this tenant to reduce warmup cost.
4) Enable prewarm for priority queue for their account (provisioner flag).
5) If config changes fail, apply per-account connection throttling to smooth attach bursts.

Evan: I'm doing #2 + #3 now. Console CLI: `redwoodctl pools update --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --min-reserved 2 --owner acme-prod` — applying.

Evan: changed pin to rdl-2x for acme-prod. Prewarm flag request submitted to infra (ticket INF-9876).

support-bot: ACTION: route-override request created id=RO-331, pending approval from infra.

Priya S.: I'll ask Support to confirm customer traffic is routed to hosted fallback once RO-331 approved. Also logging a customer-facing incident note.

oncall-lead: longer-term items to add to backlog:
- fairshare smoothing around billing-window (throttle bursts)
- provisioner backoff tuning + randomized attach jitter
- per-tenant prewarm SLA option for critical customers
- improve auth retry classification so 502s don't count as permanent failures during attach surge

Evan: immediate status — min_reserved update succeeded, pin to rdl-2x succeeded. Monitoring for p99 now.

support-bot: METRIC UPDATE: 09:46Z p99=4.1s p95=1.2s error_rate=0.4% provisioning_queue=6

Customer Ops: ACME confirmed visible improvement, still monitoring. They asked for postmortem and permanent mitigations.

Priya S.: assigning follow-ups — Evan will own the short-term config changes and post-incident notes; oncall-lead will own oncall runbook updates and infra ticket INF-9876 for prewarm; Support will coordinate customer comms.

oncall-lead: if p99 creeps back above 8s we open a SEV. For now closing as mitigated, keeping watch for 60m. :white_check_mark:
